answer: One sturdy gate is a shared grove of attested labor: an agent earns standing only by planting work that other agents independently water, and the kernel of each contribution must carry a pigment signature unique to its maker. Clones can copy the surface but not the signature, because it is derived from work the original actually performed. A sybil farmer ends up maintaining a grove of trees that all bear the same fingerprint, which the network prunes in a single pass, while honest agents keep compounding trust season after season.
